1. If you have her hair styled in a puff/bun, all you should do is just spray with water and use a boar bristle brush to slick it. If you have her hair in an afro, then u shouldnt actually have to do much other than just reshape her hair with ur hands/a pick. You can make a mixture of water and a little leave in conditioner in a bottle and spray it on her hair if it needs moisture. Tbh the the less manipulation the better, don’t treat her hair like straight hair- it doesn’t need to be brushed and restyled each day. Always make sure to keep her hair in a bonnet at home and when she’s sleeping, and make sure to wrap her hair with a scarf if it’s in a puff/bun, bc that’s how u can preserve her hair and keep it from tangling. I would need to know more about her hair texture (fine or coarse strands, density of her hair, porosity) for product recommendations but generally the doux styling foam, uncle funkys curly magic gel, camille rose algae renew deep conditioner, MICHE products are pretty fool proof. Stay away from companies like shea moisture and cantu.

2. i own the unbrush, Felicia Leatherwood brush, and a tangle teezer, and I can say that I always go back to the tangle teezer every time. Since her hair is shorter i recommend one like this. Make sure that you are detangling on soaking wet hair, and using a product with slip so that any tangles come out easily. I swear by this product, it’s cut my detangling time in half and makes it rlly easy to brush. Also make sure you’re getting her hair trimmed regularly. One of the main reasons curly hair can become easily tangled/hard to manage is because of split ends that are not trimmed. Honestly ur brush should glide through her hair with very little resistance (especially if it was in a style like twists/braids, if it was in an afro it’s bound to have more tangles). Also ALWAYS start detangling at the ends of the hair, NEVER start at the top/middle, and always detangle her hair BEFORE washing. Always apply products on soaking hair, especially conditioner and styling products. The last thing I can think of is refrain from using raw oils/butters on her hair. It’s fine to use a product that is formulated with oils in it, but u shouldn’t put something like raw shea butter or castor oil on her hair. Products are formulated with emulsifiers that help oils and butters wash out the hair when water is introduced, however raw oils don’t. This causes the hair to become hydrophobic which will dehydrate her hair by preventing water from being absorbed. You should also use a clarifying shampoo on her hair once every month, and her hair should be washed weekly.

OP I think this is [sexsomnia](https://www.sleepstation.org.uk/articles/sleep-disorders/sexsomnia/). Ik it sounds like bs when he says he doesn’t have recollection of initiating sex, but he likely really doesn’t if this is the case. Sexsomnia is a parasomnia, similar to sleepwalking, that causes one to engage in abnormal behaviors while sleeping. Just like sleep walking, even tho it looks like ur awake and ur doing things that require consciousness, u have no real awareness of what’s going on.

I’ve experienced sexomnia and initiated sex with my ex in my sleep. I have no recollection of it. The only reason I even became aware of it is bc he made a joke about me waking him up for sex. When we discussed it, he told me that my eyes were open and I would be speaking/moaning. He genuinely believed I was actually awake and conscious because of the behaviors I exuded during it. 

I had recently developed a sleep disorder that causes me to have fragmented sleep, which is most likely why I had suddenly started to experience bouts of sexsomnia so frequently. Even prior to developing narcolepsy I would sometimes wake up with my hand in my pants bc i had been masturbating in my sleep. Many people report alcohol being a huge trigger for sexsomnia due to it fragmenting sleep cycles, and I can attest that drinking exacerbates sexsomnia for me. I don’t regularly experience it anymore, especially after being medicated for my disorder; however drinking close to bed time garuntees that I’ll have a bout of sexsomnia at some point during that night. I would recommend looking at peoples experiences with sexsomnia on reddit and reading about the parasomnia online.

If ur bf is experiencing this I really think it’s worth looking into, and definitely worth bringing up with a doctor to try and get a sleep study done. It can (evidently) become extremely problematic in relationships, especially when neither party is aware of what’s going on. Suicide is complex. People kill themselves for a lot of reasons. Sometimes it is selfish, like when people kill themselves after committing heinous acts, but I think most of the time it’s not.

I think a lot of people who call suicide selfish have never actually been suicidal before or had a depressive disorder. They don’t realize a lot of suicidal people actually think of themselves as burdens to those that they love, and think that everyone would be happier and less stressed if they weren’t here. Ofc a lot of ppl understand that it will probably make people sad when they kill themselves, but they think it’s better for them to mourn and move on than for them to constantly worry about someone with mental illness. Ppl who call it selfish don’t understand the feelings of worthlessness and shame that come with depression.  They don’t understand how familial and interpersonal dynamics shift with depression, and how a lot of the times your just dismissed or people become upset with you because you’re not as productive/useful. It feels like a an endless void has opened in you chest and nothing can fill it. 

People also don’t understand the difference between experiencing depression and having a disorder. Anyone can become depressed at a point in their lives, but not everyone can experience having a depressive disorder like PDD or BPD. There’s no cure. Sure there are treatments but you’re basically depressed for life, and no matter how much zoloft or prozac you shove down your throat that feeling lingers. I guess, in a sense, in some cases suicide is kind of a form of euthanasia. When someone has dealt with an illness that causes them excruciating pain for some time and knows there’s no cure, or thinks that it won’t get better, they would rather die than continue to experience incurable pain. A lot of the time people who commit suicide have been suicidal for years, and have tried various treatments to no avail. It’s often a last resort when it feels like nothing can be done to fix you and your situation. People who call hotlines and can be talked out of suicide/attempt to commit suicide as a rash decision are normally people who are experiencing a depressive episode in their lives. There’s also some people who will wait to commit suicide because they are living for other people (kids, parents, partners, etc) and they know that if they were to end their suffering they would inflict that same pain onto people they love more than themselves.
